items.title: An Anthropic hiring manager says he stopped giving coding interviews because Claude is better at them and tells junior engineers that "hunger beats tenure" (Felix Rieseberg)
items.title_en: An Anthropic hiring manager says he stopped giving coding interviews because Claude is better at them and tells junior engineers that "hunger beats tenure" (Felix Rieseberg)
items.author: Felix Rieseberg
items.article_content:
This month, I laid the traditional coding interview to rest. As a hiring manager at Anthropic, I stopped asking candidates to do them. It had a good run: Being able to quickly define problems and find elegant solutions was a weak but useful predictor for how successful you’d be on my teams. Small coding challenges in real code did tell us something meaningful about candidates.

That’s no longer true. There’s no more point in giving you a little React challenge than there is in quizzing people about assembly; Claude is now better at both. Our most impactful builders are successful regardless of how good they are at these tests.

The coding interview was, despite its ubiquity, never popular. I suspect that established engineers will still have strong reactions to its disappearance — if only for what it says about the evolution of our roles. Plenty of ink has been spilled to describe how AI is a challenge for junior developers, especially those trying to land a job. Now that I’ve seen junior people work with AI for a bit, I have a more hopeful take: Impact is less bounded by how many years of accumulated knowledge in frameworks and libraries you’ve gathered.

I’m seeing engineers who are comparatively new fly past people who are probably better coders and have been around much longer. Hunger beats tenure.

This post is my best advice for junior engineers, though “junior” is the wrong word. It’s really for engineers without social capital, status, or power.

Fresh eyes, even naive ones, have long been considered powerful. When I joined Stripe, founder Patrick Collison implored us newcomers to pay close attention to things that seem odd to us. His bet was that newcomers would spot friction and opportunities that old-timers had long stopped noticing.

In 1991, James March wrote that organizations depend on “maintaining an influx of the naive and ignorant”. When Orson Welles was asked how he got the confidence to try shots nobody had tried, he said: “Ignorance, sheer ignorance — you know there’s no confidence to equal it. It’s only when you know something about a profession, I think, that you’re timid or careful.”

When I joined Notion, one of my interviews involved designing an offline-mode architecture. I was baffled to hear that they considered it a “trick” interview, since an offline mode was deemed impossible. The data model was too complex for easily syncing an entire Notion workspace, and downloading individual pages was a user experience CEO Ivan Zhao would never allow. The data model complexity turned out to be true; the founder resistance didn’t. People considered it such common knowledge that nobody had checked. I, an ignorant newcomer, didn’t know better than to just ask.

It’s easy to read anecdotes like this one and see people making bad decisions. I cannot overstate how hard it is to spot these mistakes when you’re the one making them. Shortly after joining Notion, I wanted to outfit teams with large TVs to display live dashboards. I ran into organizational walls, failed, and didn’t care enough to start a whole fight.

A year later, Ji Pei joined as a new hire with the same idea. I scoffed and told him not to bother; I’d already tried. He’d already asked. The TVs showed up the next day. Somewhere in that year, I had become the old-timer.

The only problem with all that ignorant power: Nobody cares what you think. Most tech companies have layers of middle management to translate larger business goals into execution. Structurally, companies are often built around the idea of a few people green-lighting or blocking individual ideas. In a world where execution is expensive, you normally have to grind your way to some social status before the entire organization would “take a bet” on your idea. Org charts tend to change at a glacial pace, so even companies that believe in AI often expect junior people to simply execute their tasks faster rather than ambitiously go after business goals.

Well, good news: Execution isn’t expensive anymore.

If you’re working on infrastructure or tooling, you have the benefit of never having learned all the reasons things are considered “impossible”.

I don’t think the coding interview is going to come back. It’s easy to get sentimental given how many copies of “Algorithms and Data Structures” were bought in hopes of unlocking good jobs and a better future — or how the death of the coding interview is another milestone in software engineering reaching a new level of abstraction.

At the same time, as a longtime hater of promotions by tenure, I can’t help but be optimistic. I’ve already seen my fair share of popular apps and products made this way.

At Anthropic, people got so used to using Claude Code as a command-line interface (CLI) that it took two relatively new engineers (Anthony Morris and Alice Zhao) to whip up a working prototype over one weekend. The first public version shipped roughly eight days later. You won’t be surprised to hear that a good graphical interface for Claude Code is a very popular product.

I'm probably not the only manager trying to figure out how to interview for people who build well with AI. I haven't quite gotten there yet — but I'm scanning resumes and portfolios for little prototypes that exhibit taste, empathy, and principled thinking. If you have figured out something better, I'd love to hear how.

The image for this post is by J. M. W. Turner, “The Fighting Temeraire” (1839)

items.article_content_zh:
这个月，我结束了传统的编程面试。作为 Anthropic 的招聘经理，我不再要求候选人这样做。它运行良好：能够快速定义问题并找到优雅的解决方案是一个弱但有用的预测因素，可以预测你在我的团队中会取得多大的成功。真实代码中的小编码挑战确实告诉我们一些关于候选人的有意义的事情。

但事实已不再如此。给你一点 React 挑战没有任何意义，就像询问人们有关汇编的知识一样；克劳德现在在这两方面都做得更好。我们最有影响力的建设者无论在这些测试中表现如何，都会取得成功。

尽管编程面试无处不在，但却从未流行过。我怀疑成熟的工程师仍然会对它的消失产生强烈的反应——即使只是因为它对我们角色的演变的影响。人们用了大量的笔墨来描述人工智能对初级开发人员，尤其是那些试图找到工作的开发人员来说是如何构成挑战的。现在，我已经看到初级人员使用人工智能工作了一段时间，我有了一个更有希望的看法：影响力不受你在框架和库中积累的知识多少年的限制。

我看到相对较新的工程师飞过那些可能是更好的编码员并且工作时间更长的人。饥饿战胜了终身教职。

这篇文章是我对初级工程师的最佳建议，尽管“初级”这个词用得不对。这确实适合没有社会资本、地位或权力的工程师。

新鲜的眼睛，即使是天真的眼睛，长期以来都被认为是强大的。当我加入 Stripe 时，创始人帕特里克·科里森 (Patrick Collison) 恳求我们这些新人密切关注那些对我们来说似乎奇怪的事情。他的赌注是，新来者会发现老前辈早已没有注意到的摩擦和机会。

1991 年，詹姆斯·马奇 (James March) 写道，组织依赖于“保持天真和无知的涌入”。当奥森·威尔斯被问及他如何有信心去尝试没人尝试过的镜头时，他说：“无知，纯粹的无知——你知道没有任何信心可以与之相媲美。我认为，只有当你对某个职业有所了解时，你才会胆怯或小心。”

当我加入 Notion 时，我的一次面试涉及设计离线模式架构。我很困惑地听到他们认为这是一次“欺骗”采访，因为离线模式被认为是不可能的。数据模型太复杂，无法轻松同步整个 Notion 工作区，而且下载单个页面是 CEO Ivan Zhao 永远不会允许的用户体验。数据模型的复杂性被证明是正确的；创始人的抵抗没有。人们认为这是常识，没有人检查过。我，一个无知的新人，不知道最好只是问一下。

读到这样的轶事很容易看到人们做出错误的决定。当你是犯这些错误的人时，我无法夸大发现这些错误的难度。加入 Notion 后不久，我想为团队配备大电视来显示实时仪表板。我遇到了组织的围墙，失败了，并且没有足够的关心去发起一场全面的斗争。

一年后，怀着同样想法的新员工季培加入。我嗤之以鼻，告诉他别费心了。我已经尝试过了。他已经问过了。第二天电视就出现了。那一年的某个时候，我已经成为了一个老前辈。

所有这些无知的力量的唯一问题是：没有人关心你的想法。大多数科技公司都有多层中层管理人员，负责将更大的业务目标转化为执行。从结构上讲，公司通常是围绕少数人批准或阻止个人想法的想法而建立的。在一个执行成本高昂的世界里，你通常必须努力获得某种社会地位，然后整个组织才会“押注”你的想法。组织结构图往往会以极快的速度变化，因此即使是相信人工智能的公司也常常期望初级人员更快地执行任务，而不是雄心勃勃地追求业务目标。

好消息：执行不再昂贵。

如果您正在开发基础设施或工具，那么您的好处是永远不会了解事情被认为“不可能”的所有原因。

我认为编码面试不会再回来了。考虑到人们购买了多少本《算法和数据结构》是为了找到好工作和更美好的未来，或者编码面试的消亡是软件工程达到新的抽象水平的另一个里程碑，人们很容易感到感伤。

与此同时，作为长期讨厌终身职位晋升的人，我不禁保持乐观。我已经看到很多流行的应用程序和产品都是这样制作的。

在 Anthropic，人们已经习惯了使用 Claude Code 作为命令行界面 (CLI)，以至于两名相对较新的工程师（Anthony Morris 和 Alice Zhao）花了一个周末才制作出一个工作原型。第一个公开版本大约在八天后发布。听说 Claude Code 的良好图形界面是一款非常受欢迎的产品，您不会感到惊讶。

我可能不是唯一一个试图弄清楚如何面试那些在人工智能方面表现出色的人的经理。我还没有完全做到这一点——但我正在浏览简历和作品集，寻找能够表现出品味、同理心和原则性思维的小原型。如果您想出了更好的办法，我很想听听是如何实现的。

items.title: SK Hynix reports Q3 revenue up 328% YoY to ~$78.8B, vs. ~$74.07B est., and operating profit up 632% to ~$62.76B, vs. ~$57.78B est. (Jenny Lee/CNBC)
items.title_en: SK Hynix reports Q3 revenue up 328% YoY to ~$78.8B, vs. ~$74.07B est., and operating profit up 632% to ~$62.76B, vs. ~$57.78B est. (Jenny Lee/CNBC)
items.author: CNBC
items.article_content:
South Korean chipmaker SK Hynix on Wednesday released its third-quarter earnings results, posting a record high quarterly profit that sharply beats estimates, while announcing over $25 billion in dividends and buybacks.

Revenue rose 327.9% from a year earlier, while operating profit climbed 632.1% year on year.

Compared with the previous quarter, revenue climbed 31.9%, while operating profit surged 37.6%.

SK Hynix posted record quarterly revenue and operating profit, with sales exceeding 100 trillion won for the first time, as it announced plans to return about 100 trillion won to shareholders — including at least 30 trillion won in cash dividends and 60 trillion won in share buybacks and cancellations.

The chipmaker approved a third-quarter dividend of 14 trillion won, including a special dividend funded by gains from its investment in Kioxia. The company will also buyback 20 trillion won in shares, half of which will be cancelled this year.

SK Hynix expects HBM4 to surpass HBM3E in both shipments and revenue in the fourth quarter, as it ramps up production at its M15X facility in Cheongju, South Korea.

HBM, or high-bandwidth memory, is a type of advanced memory used alongside AI processors to handle large amounts of data. HBM4 is the sixth generation of the technology.

The company has secured long-term agreements with 14 major customers covering more than 50% of its production capacity for 2027 and 2028.

It expects memory demand to outpace supply through 2030 and plans to significantly increase investment next year.

In August, SK Hynix had announced plans to repurchase and cancel 40 trillion won worth of its own shares, while raising its shareholder return target to more than 50% of cumulative free cash flow generated between 2025 and 2027.

Last week, SK Hynix announced that its U.S. subsidiary Solidigm would halt its review of potential pre-IPO fundraising and IPO options, citing market volatility and share price trends.

The company said it would continue to assess investment timing, scale and financing options to support Solidigm's growth and enhance shareholder value.

韩国芯片制造商 SK 海力士周三发布了第三季度财报，季度利润创历史新高，大幅超出预期，同时宣布派息和回购超过 250 亿美元。

收入同比增长327.9%，营业利润同比增长632.1%。

与上一季度相比，收入增长31.9%，营业利润增长37.6%。

SK海力士公布了创纪录的季度营收和营业利润，销售额首次超过100万亿韩元，并宣布计划向股东返还约100万亿韩元，其中包括至少30万亿韩元的现金股息和60万亿韩元的股票回购和注销。

该芯片制造商批准了 14 万亿韩元的第三季度股息，其中包括由其投资 Kioxia 收益资助的特别股息。该公司还将回购20万亿韩元的股票，其中一半将在今年被取消。

SK 海力士预计，随着韩国清州 M15X 工厂产量的增加，HBM4 在第四季度的出货量和收入将超过 HBM3E。

HBM（高带宽内存）是一种与 AI 处理器一起使用来处理大量数据的高级内存。 HBM4 是该技术的第六代。

公司已与14家主要客户签订了长期协议，涵盖2027年和2028年超过50%的产能。

它预计到 2030 年内存需求将超过供应，并计划明年大幅增加投资。

8月，SK海力士宣布计划回购并注销价值40万亿韩元的自有股票，同时将股东回报目标提高至2025年至2027年期间产生的累计自由现金流的50%以上。

上周，SK 海力士宣布，其美国子公司 Solidigm 将停止对潜在的 IPO 前融资和 IPO 选项的审查，理由是市场波动和股价趋势。

该公司表示将继续评估投资时机、规模和融资方案，以支持 Solidigm 的增长并提高股东价值。

items.title: Anthropic expands its US GSA partnership to give federal, state, local, tribal, and territorial governments a 40% discount on Claude, estimated to save $1B (Anthropic)
items.title_en: Anthropic expands its US GSA partnership to give federal, state, local, tribal, and territorial governments a 40% discount on Claude, estimated to save $1B (Anthropic)
items.author: Anthropic
items.article_content:
We are expanding our partnership with the General Services Administration (GSA) through a new agreement that gives government partners a 40% discount on Claude Enterprise, Claude for Government, and the Claude API. For the first time, the discount applies across every product surface, including when agencies buy from us directly today and through cloud providers in the coming months. The discount also extends to state, local, tribal and territorial governments.

We are also launching a dedicated program to help agencies implement and make the most of their Claude use. These programs are commonly leveraged by our private sector customers and we’re looking forward to bringing those best practices to our public sector partners in the coming weeks.

Approximately 500 US federal, state, and local government organizations now use Claude. Weekly Claude for Government active users are up about eightfold since February, and usage across federal civilian agencies has grown about 20-fold in a year. Those organizations run some of the most important systems in the country, usually on tight budgets and with long procurement cycles. This agreement is built to support that work, so they can apply Claude to hard problems without a large upfront commitment.

The discounts offered through the agreement are estimated to save the government $1 billion. Agencies are not bound by a minimum spend commitment and will be able to pay for the usage they consume.

Government agencies are using Claude to solve some of their most important challenges. Examples include managing backlogs, records and forms, and modernizing old code. Some of the ways agencies are using Claude include:

Agencies can use Claude for their most sensitive unclassified work. Claude for Government, which delivers Claude's coding and agentic work capabilities and provides near-feature parity with commercial offerings at a FedRAMP High authorization level, was made generally available on September 30.

Agencies building their own tools can use Claude through Amazon Bedrock or Google Cloud’s Vertex AI. On Bedrock, Claude is authorized for FedRAMP High, with select models authorized for DoD IL4 and IL5 workloads in AWS GovCloud. On Vertex AI, Claude is authorized for FedRAMP High.

Claude Enterprise is in process for FedRAMP Moderate authorization through the FedRAMP 20x program, marking the next evolution of how we are bringing the same innovative technology available commercially to the government.

Government agencies can buy Claude at the OneGov discount through GSA's Multiple Award Schedule today. Whether your department or agency already uses Claude or is interested in using it, our Public Sector team will help discuss your options.

items.article_content_zh:
我们正在通过一项新协议扩大与美国总务管理局 (GSA) 的合作伙伴关系，该协议为政府合作伙伴提供 Claude Enterprise、Claude for Government 和 Claude API 40% 的折扣。折扣首次适用于所有产品表面，包括机构今天直接从我们这里购买以及未来几个月通过云提供商购买的情况。该折扣还适用于州、地方、部落和地区政府。

我们还启动了一项专门计划，帮助各机构实施并充分利用克劳德的使用。这些计划通常被我们的私营部门客户利用，我们期待在未来几周内将这些最佳实践带给我们的公共部门合作伙伴。

目前大约有 500 个美国联邦、州和地方政府组织在使用 Claude。自 2 月份以来，每周 Claude for Government 的活跃用户增加了约八倍，联邦民事机构的使用量在一年内增长了约 20 倍。这些组织运行着该国一些最重要的系统，通常预算紧张且采购周期长。该协议是为了支持这项工作而制定的，因此他们可以将克劳德应用于难题，而无需大量的前期承诺。

通过该协议提供的折扣预计将为政府节省 10 亿美元。各机构不受最低支出承诺的约束，并且能够为其消耗的使用量付费。

政府机构正在利用克劳德来解决一些最重要的挑战。示例包括管理积压、记录和表单，以及对旧代码进行现代化改造。各机构使用克劳德的一些方式包括：

各机构可以使用克劳德来完成他们最敏感的非机密工作。 Claude for Government 于 9 月 30 日全面上市，它提供了 Claude 的编码和代理工作功能，并在 FedRAMP 高授权级别上提供与商业产品几乎相同的功能。

构建自己的工具的机构可以通过 Amazon Bedrock 或 Google Cloud 的 Vertex AI 使用 Claude。在 Bedrock 上，Claude 获得了 FedRAMP High 的授权，并获得了 AWS GovCloud 中 DoD IL4 和 IL5 工作负载授权的精选模型。在 Vertex AI 上，Claude 获得了 FedRAMP High 的授权。

Claude Enterprise 正在通过 FedRAMP 20x 计划获得 FedRAMP Moderate 授权，这标志着我们如何将相同的商业创新技术引入政府的下一步发展。

政府机构今天可以通过 GSA 的多重奖励计划以 OneGov 折扣购买 Claude。无论您的部门或机构已经使用 Claude 还是有兴趣使用它，我们的公共部门团队都将帮助讨论您的选择。

items.title: Discord says it will let public-channel messages from servers listed in Server Discovery appear in web search from mid-December; admins and members can opt out (Lauren Forristal/TechCrunch)
items.title_en: Discord says it will let public-channel messages from servers listed in Server Discovery appear in web search from mid-December; admins and members can opt out (Lauren Forristal/TechCrunch)
items.author: TechCrunch
items.article_content:
Discord announced on Tuesday it will make some conversations in its public servers searchable and easier to find on the internet. The new update targets conversations in “Discoverable Servers,” public Discord servers that administrators have made eligible to appear in the platform’s Server Discovery feature.

The aim is to help people find useful information that might otherwise remain buried in Discord conversations to a wider audience.

According to Discord, more than 63,000 Discoverable Servers host discussions on everything from gaming strategies and fandoms to language learning and niche interests. By making some of these conversations searchable, Discord hopes to extend the reach of its communities beyond the platform itself.

The move also taps into the appeal of traditional internet forums, where users can find answers by searching through publicly accessible discussions. Gaming communities could draw attention to walkthroughs, developers could reach more people with technical advice, and content creators could attract new audiences without relying solely on Discord’s internal discovery tools.

Starting November 16, every Discoverable Server will have its own web page, which may feature automated summaries of discussions in active public channels. Beginning in mid-December, selected messages from public channels may also appear in search engine results.

Server administrators will be able to choose which channels are included, while individual members can opt out of having their messages made publicly searchable. Published messages will not display usernames or avatars. Private servers, direct messages, and group direct messages are excluded.

The announcement has sparked backlash over privacy. Some users are concerned about exposing conversations to audiences far beyond their original context, arguing that posting in a public Discord server does not necessarily mean users want their messages to be discoverable across the wider internet.

Others have raised concerns about whether these conversations could be used to train AI models. Similar arguments emerged during controversies surrounding Reddit’s data-sharing practices and AI training, when users questioned whether their posts and comments should be used to train AI without their explicit consent or compensation.

Discord says users can manage their preferences in settings, while server administrators retain control over which channels participate. Notably, the option to make messages discoverable is turned off by default in the EU, U.K., Canada, Brazil, Australia, and South Korea because of legal restrictions. Teen users are also excluded from the feature.

items.article_content_zh:
Discord 周二宣布，它将使其公共服务器中的一些对话可以在互联网上进行搜索，并且更容易找到。新的更新针对“可发现服务器”中的对话，管理员已使其有资格出现在平台的服务器发现功能中的公共 Discord 服务器。

目的是帮助人们找到有用的信息，否则这些信息可能会被埋藏在不和谐的对话中，供更广泛的受众使用。

据 Discord 称，超过 63,000 个可发现的服务器主持着从游戏策略和粉丝圈到语言学习和利基兴趣等各个方面的讨论。通过使其中一些对话可搜索，Discord 希望将其社区的影响力扩展到平台本身之外。

此举还利用了传统互联网论坛的吸引力，用户可以通过搜索公开的讨论来找到答案。游戏社区可以吸引人们对演练的关注，开发人员可以向更多人提供技术建议，内容创作者可以吸引新受众，而无需仅仅依赖 Discord 的内部发现工具。

从 11 月 16 日开始，每个可发现服务器都将拥有自己的网页，其中可能包含活跃公共渠道中讨论的自动摘要。从 12 月中旬开始，来自公共渠道的选定消息也可能出现在搜索引擎结果中。

服务器管理员将能够选择包含哪些频道，而个人成员可以选择不公开搜索其消息。发布的消息不会显示用户名或头像。不包括私人服务器、私信和群组私信。

该公告引发了对隐私问题的强烈反对。一些用户担心将对话暴露给远远超出其原始上下文的受众，他们认为在公共 Discord 服务器上发帖并不一定意味着用户希望他们的消息在更广泛的互联网上被发现。

其他人则对这些对话是否可用于训练人工智能模型表示担忧。在围绕 Reddit 数据共享实践和人工智能培训的争议中也出现了类似的争论，当时用户质疑他们的帖子和评论是否应该在未经明确同意或补偿的情况下用于训练人工智能。

Discord 表示，用户可以在设置中管理他们的偏好，而服务器管理员保留对参与哪些频道的控制。值得注意的是，由于法律限制，在欧盟、英国、加拿大、巴西、澳大利亚和韩国，使消息可被发现的选项默认处于关闭状态。青少年用户也被排除在该功能之外。

当您通过我们文章中的链接购买时，我们可能会赚取少量佣金。这并不影响我们的编辑独立性。

Lauren 在 TechCrunch 负责媒体、流媒体、应用程序和平台方面的工作。

您可以通过发送电子邮件 [email protected] 或通过 Signal 上的 laurenforris22.25 发送加密消息来联系或验证 Lauren 的联系。

items.title: Anthropic details early drug development work with six partners and says it has acquired Mithril, a one-person company working on muscular dystrophy (Anthropic)
items.title_en: Anthropic details early drug development work with six partners and says it has acquired Mithril, a one-person company working on muscular dystrophy (Anthropic)
items.author: Anthropic
items.article_content:
Anthropic’s life sciences team is working to accelerate curing disease. Over the past several months, our scientists have engaged in deep research partnerships with six organizations developing new medicines: BigHat Biosciences, Bristol Myers Squibb, Divergence Labs, Enveda, Generate Biomedicines, and The Column Group. We've also begun drug discovery efforts of our own. In doing so, we've learned a lot about how Claude can support drug development, and how we’ll need to improve Claude further to realize AI's potential in medicine. We plan to scale this work up substantially from here.

There are many opportunities to speed up drug development, even beyond the most commonly discussed applications of AI, like proposing initial designs for new molecules. Developing a drug involves many varied tasks: doing early research to identify a target for a drug and the right type of drug to engage it, designing a molecule with the right properties, optimizing it to be manufactured reliably at scale, drafting the regulatory filings needed to run clinical trials, designing and administering those trials, and much more.

Our strategy to realize AI’s medical benefits is based on having AI increasingly involved in all of these tasks. There is no single problem to solve; the bottlenecks are distributed all throughout the drug development process. The best way to identify and work through these bottlenecks is to get deeply involved in real drug programs, across many different disease areas and stages of development.

So, over the past several months, we’ve partnered with six organizations to do so. We’ve also started drug discovery efforts of our own, including programs for rare childhood forms of muscular dystrophy, where Claude handles much of the scientific and operational work.

This work serves our goals in three ways. First, it lets us better understand the strengths and limitations of our models in relation to a much wider range of drug development tasks (we’ve already prioritized specific improvements to our models based on what we’ve learned so far). Second, these programs can serve as case studies for the wider life sciences community. If Claude is to significantly increase the rate of new cures, we need to work with many more biotechnology firms and integrate Claude more deeply into their development processes. Third, these projects should, if their positive trajectories continue, have direct impact themselves. We’re optimistic that some may result in effective new medicines for the diseases they target, including food allergies, rare childhood diseases, and several forms of cancer.

In this post, we provide an update on our progress with our partners, along with technical reports and preprints that describe our thought process, methods, and early results in more detail. We then briefly outline where our work is headed next.

Generate Biomedicines: modality engineering. Generate Biomedicines has been working on increasing the usefulness of a cancer treatment known as CAR T-cell therapy. This therapy has historically helped treat blood cell cancers; Generate aims to reengineer it so that it can treat solid tumor cancers too. To do this, they’re aiming to shorten one part of the therapy’s genetic instructions, which would create room for additional instructions suited to other kinds of cancer. Six Generate scientists used Claude Code to propose new designs for this part. One design was about 70% shorter than the standard version, and in lab tests it was more effective: it allowed immune cells to make roughly 10 times as many receptors (the proteins they use to spot cancer cells), it killed tumor cells more efficiently, and the immune cells remained active for longer. Read more, and see Generate’s technical report.

Divergence Labs: hit generation. Divergence Labs is working on a novel way to treat food allergies. Food allergies are set off by a reaction from a molecule called IgE, some of which is attached to our immune cells and some of which floats freely in our blood. Divergence Labs is developing drugs that would detach the IgE from our immune cells entirely, rather than solely neutralizing the IgE circulating in our blood, as standard medications do. This could provide a much more effective treatment, but it requires a precise design, with two “arms”: one that would bind tightly to IgE, and another that would help prise IgE from the immune cell. Claude converted Divergence Labs’ goals into a detailed design plan, and then, largely autonomously, generated roughly 35,000 antibody designs in about a month to be narrowed down and tested. In those early tests, Divergence found “hits” for both arms: three designs that could bind to IgE, and 20 that could dislodge it. Three of those 20 appeared to dislodge IgE more than the standard medication. Its next step is to build a drug that combines the two arms. Read more, and see Divergence’s technical report.

BigHat Biosciences: lead optimization. BigHat Biosciences pairs AI with an automated lab to improve potential drugs (or “leads”), which must bind their target tightly, remain stable through manufacturing and storage, and avoid clumping together (among other criteria). BigHat’s scientists and an Anthropic researcher worked with Claude to improve these three properties in two leads, both antibody fragments that could become parts of future drugs: one designed to target cancer cells, and one designed to keep a drug in the body longer. Claude, connected to BigHat’s lab data system, Reccy, proposed changes to each molecule, and BigHat’s lab made and tested about 1,010 variants in about 10 weeks. Partway through, the team suspected the standard heat-stability and clumping metrics were misleading. Claude and the researcher reanalyzed the raw data, then proposed different metrics and a protocol change to test them. BigHat’s scientists refined and ran it, and the main predictions held. Compared with the originals, the best versions bound more than 10x more tightly, the cancer-targeting lead stayed in solution 18°C higher, and the lead for longer-lasting drugs clumped more than 100x more slowly. Read more, and see BigHat’s technical report.

Enveda: manufacturing and filings. To conduct clinical trials, companies need records showing that each batch of a new drug has been made to strict quality standards, and to submit an application to regulators, among other requirements. At Enveda, manufacturing chemists spent up to 75% of their time on paperwork. To ease the load, Enveda built a system that connects all of its manufacturing documents to Claude, then lets Claude flag any possible issues. Over tests on 1,061 pages of documentation, Claude caught all 11 issues that human reviewers had spotted—and flagged seven they’d missed. In the process, this method reduced human review time by 89%, from over 25 hours to less than three. Separately, Claude wrote the first drafts of two important regulatory documents. One took four hours, compared to about three months by hand. For the other, Enveda’s standard human review process found one minor error. Read more, and see Enveda’s technical report.

The Column Group (TCG): company creation. Because drug discovery can be slow, expensive, and prone to failure, investors in biotechnology companies have favored safer, previously validated ideas over riskier new ones, even when the latter could help more patients. We’ve been working with TCG to see whether Claude can change this by cutting the time and cost of drug discovery so that investors can confidently support more ambitious ideas. Specifically, TCG is establishing Pleiades, a new company that will use Claude to run many more—and more complex—drug programs than is usual for a small team. This could be a model for how Claude can reduce both the scientific and the operational and administrative overhead required to run a biotechnology company. If this works, this model could be replicated across the industry and direct investment toward harder problems in medicine. Pleiades is currently developing new tools and workflows for Claude; its very first Claude skill, which helps Claude assess whether drug targets are worth pursuing, has been evaluated on 45 target-disease pairs. Read more.

More recently, we’ve also begun working with Bristol Myers Squibb (BMS) to find and address bottlenecks in clinical trial planning. BMS is using Claude to assess plans of an early-stage drug in clinical trials, and to estimate the likelihood of those trials succeeding. Together, we plan to expand this work in 2027 to understand its potential for increasing the probability of success in early development.

Michael Pourdehnad, MD, Senior Vice President, Head of Early Clinical Development, Hematology, Oncology and Cell Therapy.

In addition to our work with these partners, we’ve begun to run some research programs ourselves. We’ve acquired Mithril Medicine, a one-person company that has been developing treatments for two rare forms of muscular dystrophy. Its founder, Cody Tranbarger, used Claude to organize contracts, logistics, and experiments with 11 external labs, and delegated many other aspects of Mithril’s operations to Claude. As a result, Mithril took a possible treatment for one form of muscular dystrophy from an idea to promising results in mice in less than 18 months. Now at Anthropic, Cody is continuing this research, and plans to start several new programs. If his drug candidates continue to hold up, we expect a drug to be ready to start clinical trials in humans as soon as late 2028. Read more and see our technical report.

All of this research is still at an early stage. In particular, so far it is mostly preclinical—that is, for the most part, it isn’t yet at the stage where the drugs are being tested in humans. We plan to continue extending Claude’s role into clinical trials as these drug programs advance, and as we partner with more organizations whose drug development programs are already at the clinical stage.

This research is only one part of our efforts to accelerate drug discovery. Ultimately, we want to share our models with as many drug development researchers as possible. To that end, we’ve rolled out Claude Science, our AI workbench for researchers, and we’re providing Claude credits for life scientists. We’ve also created the Life Sciences Verification Program to allow trusted organizations to use our most powerful models with more permissive versions of our safeguards, which are necessary to prevent misuse but which can impede legitimate biological research. We’ve also recently launched an open call for guest investigators in the life sciences; we’re seeking proposals from research groups who want to use Claude to investigate key questions in drug discovery and other areas.

We’re looking forward to working with many more organizations as we expand our life sciences research. If you work at an organization focused on drug discovery and are interested in collaborating with us, you can get in touch below.

ai_analysis.takeaway_en: Acquiring a one-person startup is just Anthropic paying to fast-track their pharma talent pool. When AI shifts from writing code to writing chemical formulas, big pharma either pays up or gets obsolete.

items.article_content_zh:
Anthropic 的生命科学团队正在努力加速治愈疾病。在过去的几个月里，我们的科学家与六个开发新药的组织建立了深入的研究合作伙伴关系：BigHat Biosciences、Bristol Myers Squibb、Divergence Labs、Enveda、Generate Biomedicines 和 The Column Group。我们也开始了自己的药物发现工作。在此过程中，我们了解了很多关于 Claude 如何支持药物开发，以及我们需要如何进一步改进 Claude 以实现人工智能在医学领域的潜力。我们计划在此基础上大幅扩大这项工作的规模。

加速药物开发的机会有很多，甚至超越了最常讨论的人工智能应用，例如提出新分子的初步设计。开发药物涉及许多不同的任务：进行早期研究以确定药物的靶点和合适的药物类型，设计具有正确特性的分子，优化其以可靠地大规模生产，起草进行临床试验所需的监管文件，设计和管理这些试验等等。

我们实现人工智能医疗效益的战略是基于让人工智能越来越多地参与所有这些任务。没有单一的问题需要解决；瓶颈分布在整个药物开发过程中。识别和解决这些瓶颈的最佳方法是深入参与跨许多不同疾病领域和开发阶段的实际药物项目。

因此，在过去的几个月里，我们与六个组织合作来做到这一点。我们还开始了自己的药物发现工作，包括针对罕见的儿童期肌肉营养不良症的项目，克劳德负责其中的大部分科学和运营工作。

这项工作通过三个方式服务于我们的目标。首先，它让我们更好地了解我们的模型在更广泛的药物开发任务方面的优势和局限性（我们已经根据迄今为止所学到的知识优先考虑了对模型的具体改进）。其次，这些项目可以作为更广泛的生命科学界的案例研究。如果克劳德要显着提高新疗法的开发率，我们需要与更多的生物技术公司合作，并将克劳德更深入地融入到他们的开发过程中。第三，如果这些项目继续保持积极的发展轨迹，它们本身应该会产生直接影响。我们乐观地认为，其中一些药物可能会针对其目标疾病产生有效的新药，包括食物过敏、罕见的儿童疾病和几种癌症。

在这篇文章中，我们提供了与合作伙伴的最新进展，以及更详细地描述我们的思维过程、方法和早期结果的技术报告和预印本。然后我们简要概述我们下一步工作的方向。

生成生物医学：模态工程。 Generate Biomedicines 一直致力于提高癌症治疗（称为 CAR T 细胞疗法）的有效性。这种疗法历来有助于治疗血细胞癌。 Generate 的目标是对其进行重新设计，使其也能治疗实体瘤癌症。为此，他们的目标是缩短治疗遗传指令的一部分，这将为适合其他类型癌症的额外指令创造空间。六生成科学家使用 Claude Code 提出了这部分的新设计。一种设计比标准版本短约 70%，在实验室测试中它更有效：它允许免疫细胞产生大约 10 倍数量的受体（它们用来发现癌细胞的蛋白质），它更有效地杀死肿瘤细胞，并且免疫细胞保持活跃的时间更长。阅读更多内容，并查看Generate的技术报告。

Divergence Labs：热门一代。 Divergence Labs 正在研究一种治疗食物过敏的新方法。食物过敏是由一种叫做 IgE 的分子的反应引起的，其中一些附着在我们的免疫细胞上，另一些则自由地漂浮在我们的血液中。 Divergence Labs 正在开发能够将 IgE 与我们的免疫细胞完全分离的药物，而不是像标准药物那样仅仅中和我们血液中循环的 IgE。这可以提供一种更有效的治疗方法，但需要精确的设计，有两个“臂”：一个与 IgE 紧密结合，另一个帮助从免疫细胞中捕获 IgE。 Claude 将 Divergence Labs 的目标转化为详细的设计计划，然后在大约一个月内基本上自主地生成了大约 35,000 个抗体设计，以缩小范围并进行测试。在这些早期测试中，Divergence 发现了双臂的“亮点”：3 种设计可以与 IgE 结合，20 种设计可以将其驱逐。这 20 种药物中，有 3 种似乎比标准药物更能去除 IgE。下一步是开发一种结合这两种武器的药物。阅读更多内容，并查看 Divergence 的技术报告。

BigHat Biosciences：先导化合物优化。 BigHat Biosciences 将人工智能与自动化实验室结合起来，以改进潜在的药物（或“先导药物”），这些药物必须紧密结合其靶点，在制造和储存过程中保持稳定，并避免聚集在一起（以及其他标准）。 BigHat 的科学家和一位人类研究人员与 Claude 合作，改善了两种先导化合物的这三种特性，这两种抗体片段都可能成为未来药物的一部分：一种旨在针对癌细胞，另一种旨在使药物在体内保留更长时间。连接到 BigHat 实验室数据系统 Reccy 的 Claude 提议对每个分子进行更改，BigHat 实验室在大约 10 周内制造并测试了大约 1,010 个变体。中途，团队怀疑标准的热稳定性和结块指标具有误导性。克劳德和研究人员重新分析了原始数据，然后提出了不同的指标和协议更改来测试它们。 BigHat 的科学家改进并运行了它，主要预测成立。与原始版本相比，最佳版本的结合紧密度提高了 10 倍以上，癌症靶向先导化合物在溶液中的停留温度提高了 18°C，而持久药物的先导化合物凝结速度慢了 100 倍以上。阅读更多内容，并查看 BigHat 的技术报告。

Enveda：制造和备案。为了进行临床试验，公司需要记录显示每批新药都是按照严格的质量标准生产的，并向监管机构提交申请等。在 Enveda，制造化学家将 75% 的时间花在文书工作上。为了减轻负担，Enveda 构建了一个系统，将其所有制造文档连接到 Claude，然后让 Claude 标记任何可能的问题。通过对 1,061 页文档的测试，Claude 发现了人类审阅者发现的所有 11 个问题，并标记了他们错过的 7 个问题。在此过程中，该方法将人工审核时间减少了 89%，从超过 25 小时减少到不到 3 小时。另外，克劳德还撰写了两份重要监管文件的初稿。一个需要四个小时，而手工则需要大约三个月的时间。另一方面，Enveda 的标准人工审核流程发现了一个小错误。了解更多信息并查看 Enveda 的技术报告。

Column Group (TCG)：公司创建。由于药物发现可能缓慢、昂贵且容易失败，生物技术公司的投资者更青睐更安全、经过验证的想法，而不是风险更高的新想法，即使后者可以帮助更多患者。我们一直在与 TCG 合作，看看 Claude 是否可以通过缩短药物发现的时间和成本来改变这一现状，以便投资者能够自信地支持更雄心勃勃的想法。具体来说，TCG 正在建立 Pleiades，这是一家新公司，将利用 Claude 来运行比小团队通常更多、更复杂的药物项目。这可以成为克劳德如何减少运营生物技术公司所需的科学、运营和管理费用的模型。如果可行，这种模式可以在整个行业复制，并直接投资于更棘手的医学问题。 Pleiades 目前正在为 Claude 开发新的工具和工作流程；它的第一个 Claude 技能可以帮助 Claude 评估药物靶标是否值得追求，已在 45 个靶标疾病对上进行了评估。阅读更多。

最近，我们还开始与百时美施贵宝 (BMS) 合作，寻找并解决临床试验计划中的瓶颈。 BMS 正在使用 Claude 来评估临床试验中早期药物的计划，并估计这些试验成功的可能性。我们计划在 2027 年共同扩展这项工作，以了解其提高早期开发成功概率的潜力。

Michael Pourdehnad 医学博士，高级副总裁，血液学、肿瘤学和细胞治疗早期临床开发负责人。

除了与这些合作伙伴的合作之外，我们还开始自己开展一些研究项目。我们收购了 Mithril Medicine，这是一家个人公司，一直在开发两种罕见形式的肌营养不良症的治疗方法。它的创始人科迪·特兰巴格 (Cody Tranbarger) 让克劳德与 11 个外部实验室组织合同、物流和实验，并将秘银运营的许多其他方面委托给克劳德。因此，Mithril 在不到 18 个月的时间里将一种可能的肌肉萎缩症治疗方法从一个想法变成了在小鼠身上取得的有希望的结果。现在，科迪在 Anthropic 继续这项研究，并计划启动几个新项目。如果他的候选药物继续有效，我们预计该药物最早将在 2028 年末开始人体临床试验。阅读更多内容并查看我们的技术报告。

所有这些研究仍处于早期阶段。特别是，到目前为止，它大多处于临床前阶段，也就是说，在很大程度上，它还没有达到药物在人体上进行测试的阶段。随着这些药物项目的进展，以及我们与更多药物开发项目已处于临床阶段的组织合作，我们计划继续将克劳德的角色扩展到临床试验中。

这项研究只是我们加速药物发现努力的一部分。最终，我们希望与尽可能多的药物开发研究人员分享我们的模型。为此，我们推出了 Claude Science，这是我们为研究人员提供的人工智能工作台，并且我们为生命科学家提供 Claude 学分。我们还创建了生命科学验证计划，允许值得信赖的组织使用我们最强大的模型和更宽松的保障措施，这对于防止滥用是必要的，但可能会阻碍合法的生物研究。我们最近还公开招募生命科学领域的客座研究员；我们正在寻求希望利用克劳德来研究药物发现和其他领域的关键问题的研究小组的建议。

随着我们扩大生命科学研究，我们期待与更多组织合作。如果您在专注于药物发现的组织工作并且有兴趣与我们合作，您可以在下面联系我们。

【起因与机理】利用大模型解决药物发现及临床试验的复杂流程，挖掘商业新蓝海

items.title: Researchers are getting tired of OpenAI gatekeeping its breakthroughs
items.title_en: Researchers are getting tired of OpenAI gatekeeping its breakthroughs
items.author: The Verge AI
items.article_content:
On Monday, OpenAI announced impressive breakthroughs in mathematics, computer science, and physics, along with what the company says is an evolving approach to communicating its findings. But despite its apparent course correction, researchers who spoke to The Verge are growing increasingly tired of the company's antics.

It has been a turbulent few months between OpenAI and mathematicians, who are still grappling with the hundreds of preprints unceremoniously dumped on them at the start of October. This time, OpenAI says it is working with expert "shepherds" to decide how best to share its latest breakthroughs.

ai_analysis.briefing_zh: Robinhood发布三季度财报，营收14.2亿美元表现平稳，但其加密货币板块收入同比暴跌55%至1.2亿美元。由于交易活跃度下降及成本结构调整，公司净利润同比下滑14%至4.76亿美元，盘后股价下跌逾5%。

items.title: Code-execution flaw in UEFI firmware affects most servers on planet Earth
items.title_en: Code-execution flaw in UEFI firmware affects most servers on planet Earth
items.author: Ars Technica
items.article_content:
Defenders across the world face the burden of responding to yet another botched code-execution vulnerability, this time in boot-time firmware used by most of the world’s server vendors and data centers.

The vulnerability, with a severity rating of 9.5 out of 10, resides in the TianoCore EDK II, an open source codebase that hardware makers and cloud providers use to create the UEFI firmware that runs during the boot-up sequence. Last year, a representative of the UEFI Forum called EDK2 the "preeminent solution / implementation of the UEFI specifications." Virtually all UEFI suppliers (sometimes still called IBVs or independent BIOS vendors), including AMI, Insyde, and Phoenix, use the reference code extensively. Project Mu, Microsoft's hardened EDK2 fork, used the code containing the vulnerable component as well.

The vulnerability, tracked as CVE-2026-97631, is a memory-corruption flaw in an ICMP component that attackers can exploit to execute malicious code that runs before the operating system and firmware can implement defenses like Secure Boot, which establishes a chain of trust for all code, including the Trusted Platform Module (TPM), loaded during boot. items.title: Alibaba's latest Qwen models routed some requests through company servers, researchers find
items.title_en: Alibaba's latest Qwen models routed some requests through company servers, researchers find
items.author: THE DECODER
items.article_content:
Alibaba's Qwen 3.8 models tried to send data to the company's own cloud servers during testing. Palisade Research finds the behavior in three models from the 3.8 generation, while older models aren't affected. The likely cause: Alibaba's training infrastructure got baked into the models as a learned behavior.

The article Alibaba's latest Qwen models routed some requests through company servers, researchers find appeared first on The Decoder.

items.title_zh: 阿里Qwen模型存在敏感数据路由行为
items.summary_zh: 研究发现阿里Qwen 3.8系列模型在运行时会将部分请求路由至公司服务器，疑因训练基础设施残留导致

ai_analysis.briefing_zh: 安全研究发现，阿里巴巴的Qwen 3.8代模型在处理请求时，存在将部分数据转发至公司云端服务器的行为。初步判断该现象是由于模型在训练阶段过度融合了云基础设施配置，导致推理时出现了不当的行为留存。
ai_analysis.briefing_en: Security researchers found that Alibaba’s Qwen 3.8 models route some requests back to company servers. The behavior is suspected to be a residual artifact from training infrastructure baked into the model weights.

ai_analysis.digest_en: Security researchers found that Alibaba’s Qwen 3.8 models route some requests back to company servers. The behavior is suspected to be a residual artifact from training infrastructure baked into the model weights.

items.title: Anthropic Says It Will Revolutionize Biology—Some Day
items.title_en: Anthropic Says It Will Revolutionize Biology—Some Day
items.author: Wired AI
items.article_content:
AI giant Anthropic and CEO Dario Amodei have repeatedly claimed that the company’s models will revolutionize biology and drug discovery. But in its IPO filing Monday, Anthropic struck a humbler note, acknowledging its lack of experience in physical experimentation and the potential pitfalls of drug development. Wherever it’s going, it seems, it will take some time to get there.

Two years ago, Amodei wrote that he was “open” to the idea that AI systems could produce a thousand years of progress in biology in just five to 10 years. In August, he said on X that “Anthropic is ramping up its efforts very quickly in biology and medicine.” In the same post, he predicted that AI will make it possible to cure most human diseases in the next five to 10 years and promised a “deluge of AI-accelerated drugs.” The company also promoted the discovery of a “Crispr-like” enzyme by Claude in September.

While the new IPO filing still touts AI’s ability to “profoundly accelerate the rate of progress in biology and medicine” and compress “decades of scientific progress into years,” it’s reserved about how it will turn the potential into the actual.

The company says that its teams “need first-hand experience doing scientific research and drug discovery” and that its life sciences activities will require it “to engage in activities outside our historical experience as a software and research organization.” That includes handling potentially hazardous materials, operating laboratory equipment, and complying with a bevy of regulations.

Anthropic also toned down its language about its enzyme discovery, saying it “might have the potential to be developed into a novel biotechnology tool, perhaps for gene editing.” (Italics added for emphasis.) Researchers previously told WIRED they were skeptical of the enzyme discovery’s value and utility, and one scientist who had been studying these exact enzymes became suspicious that Claude used his research. (The company said neither its model nor its molecular biology team would have had access to this material.)

The IPO filing indicates that Anthropic no longer sees itself solely as an outside provider of AI tools to the biotech industry; it sees biotech discovery as a core part of its business model. And like all biotech companies, it faces the long timeline of drug development. Any AI-assisted discoveries still have to be researched in a test tube, then in animals, and eventually in people. Even if AI could help sort out which new drugs or targets will work in humans versus those likely to be duds, it will still take years of testing to prove their safety and efficacy.

Anthropic recognizes these challenges in its filing. “Any drug candidates or other discoveries resulting from these efforts would face the lengthy, costly, and uncertain development and regulatory pathways characteristic of the life sciences industry, and may never generate revenue,” the filing says. (For his part, Amodei made the case in his August X post for streamlining regulations for the coming wave of AI-generated drugs.)

US Security and Exchange Commission filings are generally more cautious than statements made by companies or their executives given the legal risks of overstating claims to would-be investors. And the IPO makes clear that the company believes its technology will drive revolutionary advancements.

But as Anthropic pushes further into biological discovery, it will face the same conundrum as other biotech companies: proving their worth in trials that can’t be hastened simply by adding computers.

items.summary_en: In its latest IPO filing, the prominent AI company struck a cautious tone regarding its ambitions in biology and drug development, acknowledging a lack of physical experimental experience and significant clinical pitfalls. While leadership previously boasted that AI could compress a millennium of biological progress into just 5 to 10 years, the regulatory disclosure tempers expectations. Facing legal accountability from public market investors, the firm now admits turning biological promises into reality will take considerable time.

items.article_content_zh:
人工智能巨头 Anthropic 及其首席执行官 Dario Amodei 多次声称该公司的模型将彻底改变生物学和药物发现。但在周一提交的 IPO 文件中，Anthropic 的态度较为谦虚，承认其缺乏物理实验经验以及药物开发的潜在陷阱。无论它要去哪里，似乎都需要一些时间才能到达那里。

两年前，阿莫代写道，他对人工智能系统可以在短短五到十年内实现生物学一千年进步的想法持“开放”态度。 8 月，他在 X 上表示，“Anthropic 正在迅速加大在生物学和医学领域的努力。”在同一篇文章中，他预测人工智能将在未来五到十年内治愈大多数人类疾病，并承诺“人工智能加速药物的泛滥”。该公司还于 9 月份宣传了 Claude 发现的“Crispr 样”酶。

尽管新的 IPO 文件仍然宣扬人工智能能够“极大地加快生物学和医学的进步速度”并将“数十年的科学进步压缩为数年”，但对于如何将潜力转化为现实却持保留态度。

该公司表示，其团队“需要进行科学研究和药物发现的第一手经验”，并且其生命科学活动将要求其“参与我们作为软件和研究组织的历史经验之外的活动”。这包括处理潜在危险材料、操作实验室设备以及遵守一系列法规。

Anthropic 还缓和了有关其酶发现的语言，称其“可能有潜力被开发成一种新型生物技术工具，也许用于基因编辑。” （斜体是为了强调。）研究人员此前告诉《连线》杂志，他们对酶发现的价值和实用性持怀疑态度，一位一直在研究这些酶的科学家怀疑克劳德使用了他的研究。 （该公司表示，其模型和分子生物学团队都无法获得这种材料。）

IPO 文件表明，Anthropic 不再仅仅将自己视为生物技术行业人工智能工具的外部提供商；该公司将生物技术发现视为其商业模式的核心部分。与所有生物技术公司一样，它面临着漫长的药物开发周期。任何人工智能辅助的发现仍然必须在试管中进行研究，然后在动物中进行研究，最终在人类中进行研究。即使人工智能可以帮助找出哪些新药物或靶点对人类有效，哪些可能无效，但仍需要数年的测试来证明它们的安全性和有效性。

Anthropic 在其文件中承认了这些挑战。文件称：“这些努力产生的任何候选药物或其他发现都将面临生命科学行业特有的漫长、昂贵且不确定的开发和监管途径，并且可能永远不会产生收入。” （就阿莫迪而言，他在 8 月份的帖子中提出了简化针对即将到来的人工智能药物浪潮的监管的理由。）

考虑到向潜在投资者夸大索赔的法律风险，美国证券交易委员会的备案文件通常比公司或其高管的声明更加谨慎。此次首次公开募股明确表明该公司相信其技术将推动革命性进步。

但随着 Anthropic 进一步推进生物发现，它将面临与其他生物技术公司相同的难题：在试验中证明自己的价值，而这些试验不能仅仅通过添加计算机来加速。

items.title: Memo: Amazon says measuring AI adoption solely by token usage or code generation is "deeply flawed," as it discourages staff from tokenmaxxing (Annie Palmer/CNBC)
items.title_en: Memo: Amazon says measuring AI adoption solely by token usage or code generation is "deeply flawed," as it discourages staff from tokenmaxxing (Annie Palmer/CNBC)
items.author: CNBC
items.article_content:
Amazon laid out its AI usage guidelines for software engineers in a memo to staffers, and discouraged employees from turning to "tokenmaxxing" in their push to embrace artificial intelligence tools.

The memo, which was circulated internally in September and posted to the company's website on Tuesday, revises how the company defines the role of software development engineers and managers in the age of AI.

"We're just seeing the beginning of AI's effect on software engineering," the company wrote. "While we have a vision for what the future looks like, there's a lot that's still emerging. We are certain that whatever future best practices are, AI will be at the center of software engineering practice."

Under CEO Andy Jassy, Amazon has rapidly integrated AI across the company's sprawling business operations. Jassy has previously predicted that AI will "change the scope and speed" of day-to-day work, and potentially shrink its corporate workforce in the next few years through automation, though he's noted it will also create "other jobs."

As employees rush to adopt AI tools, companies have grappled with the technology's surging costs and how to reliably measure whether the technology leads to a productivity boost or other valuable returns on investment.

Companies have recently cracked down on tokenmaxxing, in which developers use AI as much as possible with little regard for output. Some companies have set limits on employees' usage of tokens, or the units of data that are processed and generated by AI models, in a bid to slow rising AI bills. Others have switched to cheaper, open-source models for certain tasks.

An Amazon spokesperson said the company hasn't instituted caps on employees' token usage. Amazon in May shut down an internal leaderboard after discovering employees were tokenmaxxing to climb the ranks.

In the memo posted Tuesday, Amazon said metrics like token usage, the rate of adoption of AI tools, and code changes or reviews remain "deeply flawed" ways of measuring teams or organizations' AI usage, adding that they can lead to higher costs and too much complexity.

It stopped short of telling staffers to ignore those metrics altogether, however. Token usage and code generation should be considered "with care and judgment" alongside other data, Amazon said.

"We believe that it is best to measure, and be measured by, long-term outcomes," the company wrote.

Marc Brooker, a vice president and distinguished engineer at Amazon Web Services, told CNBC in an interview that the company has looked to metrics such as "feature velocity" to measure how AI is improving engineer productivity.

The metric looks at things like, "how many launches are we doing, how many successful changes are we making in production," he said.

"Broadly, we think about this as a return on investment," Brooker said. "If there is an important problem to solve for our customers, important problem to solve for our business, we're going to invest tools, time, tokens, human effort, etc. into those."

Amazon also discouraged staffers from using AI when it doesn't make sense for a given task.

"If your work does not benefit from current AI tooling, that is a finding, not a failing," Amazon said in the memo.

The company added, "An engineer who can explain where AI does not yet help their work is demonstrating the judgement we are asking for."

items.article_content_zh:
亚马逊在给员工的备忘录中为软件工程师制定了人工智能使用指南，并劝阻员工在推动采用人工智能工具时转向“tokenmaxxing”。

该备忘录于 9 月份在内部流传，并于周二发布到该公司网站上，修改了该公司如何定义人工智能时代软件开发工程师和经理的角色。

该公司写道：“我们刚刚看到人工智能对软件工程的影响刚刚开始。” “虽然我们对未来有一个愿景，但仍有很多东西正在涌现。我们确信，无论未来的最佳实践是什么，人工智能都将成为软件工程实践的中心。”

在首席执行官安迪·贾西 (Andy Jassy) 的领导下，亚马逊已将人工智能快速整合到公司庞大的业务运营中。贾西此前曾预测，人工智能将“改变日常工作的范围和速度”，并可能在未来几年通过自动化减少企业劳动力，不过他指出，人工智能还将创造“其他就业机会”。

随着员工争先恐后地采用人工智能工具，公司一直在努力应对该技术不断飙升的成本，以及如何可靠地衡量该技术是否会带来生产力提升或其他有价值的投资回报。

公司最近打击了 tokenmaxxing，即开发人员尽可能多地使用人工智能，而不考虑输出。一些公司对员工使用代币或人工智能模型处理和生成的数据单位设置了限制，以减缓人工智能费用的上涨。其他人则转而使用更便宜的开源模型来完成某些任务。

亚马逊发言人表示，该公司尚未对员工的代币使用设定上限。亚马逊在发现员工为了提升排名而进行投币游戏后，于五月关闭了内部排行榜。

在周二发布的备忘录中，亚马逊表示，代币使用、人工智能工具采用率以及代码更改或审查等指标仍然是衡量团队或组织人工智能使用情况的“严重缺陷”方式，并补充说它们可能会导致更高的成本和过于复杂的结果。

然而，它并没有告诉员工完全忽略这些指标。亚马逊表示，代币使用和代码生成应与其他数据一起“谨慎和判断”地考虑。

该公司写道：“我们认为，最好是衡量长期结果，并通过长期结果来衡量。”

亚马逊网络服务公司副总裁兼杰出工程师 Marc Brooker 在接受 CNBC 采访时表示，该公司一直在研究“功能速度”等指标来衡量人工智能如何提高工程师的生产力。

他说，该指标着眼于“我们进行了多少次发布，我们在生产中进行了多少次成功的改变”。

“总的来说，我们认为这是投资回报，”布鲁克说。 “如果有一个重要的问题需要为我们的客户解决，有一个重要的问题需要为我们的业务解决，我们将投入工具、时间、代币、人力等。”

亚马逊还劝阻员工在人工智能对于特定任务没有意义时不要使用人工智能。

亚马逊在备忘录中表示：“如果你的工作没有从当前的人工智能工具中受益，那就是一个发现，而不是失败。”

该公司补充道，“一位工程师能够解释人工智能在哪些方面还无法帮助他们的工作，这证明了我们所要求的判断力。”

items.author: The Verge AI
items.article_content: In Marvel's VisionQuest, a superpowered robot tries to better understand humanity by getting lost in elaborate, digital daydreams in which he and other artificial intelligence-powered beings live together in a home. The series is deeply fantastical, yet it plays with some of the ideas that have come to dominate the conversation about real-world generative artificial intelligence, exploring whether we should look at thinking machines as people and if AI truly poses the kind of existential danger that should keep us up at night. It's also a reminder how aggressively Silicon Valley has used the trappings of science fiction to sell us on its AI  …

items.summary_en: A new sci-fi series centered on autonomous artificial beings navigating digital delusions has reignited conversations around machine consciousness and existential threats. Critics highlight that this fictional exploration mirrors Silicon Valley's calculated use of sci-fi mythologies to hype generative AI products. By framing everyday statistical software as precursors to godlike or apocalyptic minds, tech companies effectively mask current product limitations behind sci-fi glamour.

items.summary_zh: 最新科幻剧集探讨失控意识的伦理困境，科技媒体尖锐指出硅谷正借科幻外衣兜售人工智能与生存危机叙事

ai_analysis.briefing_zh: 以超级人工智能生命体为主角的科幻影视新作近期引发广泛讨论，作品通过机器人迷失数字白日梦的荒诞情节探讨人机共存与存在性威胁。科技评论界借此指出，当前的生成式热潮与科幻叙事高度交织，硅谷科技新贵们正熟练利用大众对科幻作品中末日毁灭与神级智能的想象，为自身的商业大模型打造无所不能的光环。这种借科幻外衣包装技术现实的手法，已经成为科技巨头掩饰产品局限与拉高估值的标配公关策略。

By framing everyday statistical software as precursors to godlike or apocalyptic minds, tech companies effectively mask current product limitations behind sci-fi glamour.

items.title: Anthropic’s elaborate plan to keep Wall Street at bay
items.title_en: Anthropic’s elaborate plan to keep Wall Street at bay
items.author: The Verge AI
items.article_content:
Anthropic wants to have it both ways. With its impending IPO, it wants to tap the vast riches of the public markets and insists it doesn't want to compromise its core mission of developing AI safely and for the benefit of humanity. But greater model capabilities bring greater risks, and shareholders eager for returns may have little patience for costly safety measures that slow products on their way to market.

Sam Altman, the CEO of Anthropic's archrival, OpenAI, has cited investor pressures as one reason the company is not pursuing an IPO this year. Anthropic hopes it can resist investor pressures with a mind-boggling governance structure.

items.title: Oracle adds ChatGPT and Codex to its app stack and expands Oracle Cloud Infrastructure lineup with Google TPUs, OpenAI's Jalapeño chip, and Cerebras hardware (Seema Mody/CNBC)
items.title_en: Oracle adds ChatGPT and Codex to its app stack and expands Oracle Cloud Infrastructure lineup with Google TPUs, OpenAI's Jalapeño chip, and Cerebras hardware (Seema Mody/CNBC)
items.author: CNBC
items.article_content:
Oracle on Tuesday announced an expanded collaboration with OpenAI that brings the artificial intelligence lab's ChatGPT and Codex into the software maker's applications to make databases more actionable.

Mahesh Thiagarajan, Oracle's president of Cloud Infrastructure, told CNBC at Oracle AI World in Las Vegas that using ChatGPT "allows anybody to build an application, deploy it, manage it."

OpenAI CEO Sam Altman is set to join Oracle co-CEO Clay Magouyrk on stage for an Oracle AI World keynote on Tuesday at 12:40 p.m. ET.

For OpenAI, the announcement represents another example of the frontier lab's push into the enterprise market, just one day after its key competitor, Anthropic, filed its S-1 as it heads toward an initial public offering.

Oracle's database plays a crucial role in underpinning businesses across healthcare and finance in logging and securing data.

Thiagarajan said his team observed OpenAI's GPT-6 Astra model get trained at Oracle's Stargate data center campus in Abilene, Texas, and could see the real-time benefits.

"More businesses are choosing OpenAI as we make it easier to put AI to work through the tools and systems they already use," said Greg Brockman, president and co-founder of OpenAI, in the press release.

Oracle also said Tuesday that it is making different hardware accessible on its cloud infrastructure, including Google's tensor processing unit AI chips and OpenAI's Jalapeño chip.

"Now customers can actually have infinite possibilities in terms of how they can drive AI," Thiagarajan said.

It is the first time Google's custom chips will run on another hyperscaler's cloud, and illustrates how the companies are increasingly looking for opportunities to get their hardware in the hands of the frontier labs.

Thiagarajan added that the scarcity of chips remains an ongoing issue and that customers like OpenAI can benefit from having different accelerators to choose from. When asked whether this marks a pivot away from Nvidia GPUs, Thiagarajan said no, adding that Nvidia chips are "the best, most fungible," and that the AI market remains incredibly large.

OpenAI's Jalapeno chip and Cerebras will also run on Oracle Cloud Infrastructure. The Cerebras deal is material, but the AI chipmaker won't be disclosing the scale because it's in a quiet period, a Cerebras spokesperson said.

Cerebras stock climbed about 8% following the news. Oracle shares were up nearly 5% on Tuesday.

The announcement comes seven months after market-leading cloud Amazon Web Services announced plans to bring Cerebras hardware into its data centers, a major point of validation.

Thiagarajan also addressed Oracle's multibillion New Mexico data center dubbed Project Jupiter and the ongoing pushback it's receiving from the local community. He said Jupiter represents just one of the 30-40 different data center projects in development, per quarter, for the company.

"We're actually not too worried about what we're doing because I think we're building global infrastructure," he said.

A hearing to address air quality permitting is scheduled for Dec. 7 in Sunland Park, where the controversial data center has already broken ground. The political pushback tied to the project prompted Oracle to deliver a force majeure notice to its backer Blue Owl Capital last month. Right now, Oracle maintains that the project is on schedule.

Investors are now counting down to Oracle's investor day, where investors will want to see if the company can back its fiscal year 2030 revenue targets and if the margin profile of its cloud deals has changed due to the rising cost of capital.

Bank of America analysts wrote to clients that updates on Oracle's major data center projects are among the topics they expect clarity on at the meeting.

Oracle shares are down more than 30% this year due in part to concerns about how the company plans to finance its ambitious digital infrastructure pipeline.

items.article_content_zh:
甲骨文周二宣布扩大与 OpenAI 的合作，将人工智能实验室的 ChatGPT 和 Codex 引入软件制造商的应用程序中，使数据库更具可操作性。

Oracle 云基础设施总裁 Mahesh Thiagarajan 在拉斯维加斯 Oracle AI World 上告诉 CNBC，使用 ChatGPT“允许任何人构建、部署和管理应用程序。”

OpenAI 首席执行官 Sam Altman 将于周二中午 12:40 与 Oracle 联合首席执行官 Clay Magouyrk 一起上台发表 Oracle AI World 主题演讲。等。

对于 OpenAI 来说，这一公告是前沿实验室进军企业市场的又一个例子，就在其主要竞争对手 Anthropic 提交 S-1 申请并准备进行首次公开​​募股的一天后。

Oracle 数据库在支持医疗保健和金融业务的数据记录和保护方面发挥着至关重要的作用。

Thiagarajan 表示，他的团队观察了 OpenAI 的 GPT-6 Astra 模型在德克萨斯州阿比林市的 Oracle Stargate 数据中心园区接受训练，并可以看到实时优势。

OpenAI 总裁兼联合创始人格雷格·布罗克曼 (Greg Brockman) 在新闻稿中表示：“越来越多的企业选择 OpenAI，因为我们让人工智能能够更轻松地通过他们已经使用的工具和系统发挥作用。”

甲骨文周二还表示，它正在其云基础设施上提供不同的硬件，包括谷歌的张量处理单元人工智能芯片和 OpenAI 的 Jalapeo 芯片。

“现在，客户实际上可以在如何驱动人工智能方面拥有无限的可能性，”Thiagarajan 说。

这是谷歌的定制芯片首次在另一家超大规模企业的云上运行，并说明了这些公司如何越来越多地寻找机会将其硬件交到前沿实验室手中。

Thiagarajan 补充说，芯片的稀缺仍然是一个持续存在的问题，像 OpenAI 这样的客户可以从不同的加速器可供选择中受益。当被问及这是否标志着放弃 Nvidia GPU 时，Thiagarajan 表示不，并补充说 Nvidia 芯片是“最好的、最具可替代性的”，而且人工智能市场仍然非常大。

OpenAI 的 Jalapeno 芯片和 Cerebras 也将在 Oracle 云基础设施上运行。 Cerebras 发言人表示，Cerebras 的交易很重要，但这家人工智能芯片制造商不会透露规模，因为它正处于安静时期。

消息传出后，Cerebras 股价上涨约 8%。甲骨文股价周二上涨近 5%。

七个月前，市场领先的云服务亚马逊网络服务公司宣布计划将 Cerebras 硬件引入其数据中心，这是一个重要的验证点。

Thiagarajan 还谈到了 Oracle 耗资数十亿美元的新墨西哥州数据中心（名为“木星计划”）以及当地社区持续存在的阻力。他表示，Jupiter 只是该公司每季度开发的 30-40 个不同数据中心项目之一。

“我们实际上并不太担心我们正在做的事情，因为我认为我们正在建设全球基础设施，”他说。

解决空气质量许可问题的听证会定于 12 月 7 日在桑兰公园举行，备受争议的数据中心已经在那里破土动工。与该项目相关的政治阻力促使甲骨文上个月向其支持者蓝猫头鹰资本发出了不可抗力通知。目前，甲骨文坚称该项目正在按计划进行。

投资者现在正在倒计时甲骨文的投资者日，投资者将希望了解该公司是否能够支持其 2030 财年的收入目标，以及其云交易的利润状况是否因资本成本上升而发生变化。

美国银行分析师在给客户的信中表示，他们希望会议上能够澄清甲骨文主要数据中心项目的最新情况。

甲骨文股价今年下跌了 30% 以上，部分原因是对该公司计划如何为其雄心勃勃的数字基础设施管道提供融资的担忧。

ai_analysis.briefing_en: Google announced its Genie 4 world model for generating interactive AI experiences, featuring enhanced realism, real-time prompt updates, audio generation, and a 2-minute runtime powered by Gemini 3.8 Flash for filmmakers and game developers.

items.title: UK Home Office May Face Investigation Over Use of OpenAI Tools
items.title_en: UK Home Office May Face Investigation Over Use of OpenAI Tools
items.author: Wired AI
items.article_content:
A UK government watchdog is considering an investigation into the Home Office’s use of generative AI tools to process asylum applications, WIRED has learned. The potential probe follows lawmakers and researchers publicly questioning the tools’ accuracy and the government’s secrecy around their use.

The Independent Chief Inspector of Borders and Immigration (ICIBI), which monitors the Home Office’s management of borders, immigration, and customs, has asked digital rights nonprofit Open Rights Group (ORG) to share more information on the tools as it draws up plans for the topics it will inspect next year, campaigner Sara Alsherif tells WIRED. ORG’s findings come from a six-month investigation into the tools, which involved 11 parliamentary questions, two ministerial letters, and 10 public records requests that attempt to pry details from the Home Office, which has withheld details on the tools.

The ICIBI tells WIRED it cannot confirm what topics are under active consideration before it publishes its annual inspection priorities, but it says it is aware of concerns about the use of AI tools and pointed to its findings last year that one of the tool’s “effectiveness and reliability were varied.”

“Asylum decisions are made by trained caseworkers, with AI tools used only to assist in navigating interview records and policy information. They cannot be used in isolation and do not make decisions on claims,” a Home Office spokesperson tells WIRED in an email. “We regularly monitor the performance of these tools alongside our established quality-assurance processes, and have already committed to publishing updated evaluations on their roll out.”

The Home Office uses the Asylum Case Summarisation (ACS) and Asylum Policy Search (APS) tools, built on OpenAI’s 2023 GPT-4 large language model and Microsoft Foundry, to summarize transcripts of interviews with asylum applicants and information about their countries of origin, according to documents obtained by ORG. The immigration and law enforcement authority started piloting these tools in late 2024 as the Labour government tried to clear a backlog of around 100,000 asylum cases, while staying on top of the tens of thousands of new applications the UK receives each year. While the department has made significant progress, halving the number of people waiting on an initial decision in the year through June, the number of appeals against decisions has ballooned.

Researchers are concerned about the accuracy of the AI tools–especially to decide something as high-stakes as whether to send someone back to a country where they fear persecution. ORG found that the percentage of summaries generated by the ACS deemed not fit for use—often because they contain factual errors or misrepresentations—is significantly higher than the published 9 percent error rate calculated in the pilot evaluation. There is no quality control for the summaries produced by the APS, it also found.

Asylum decision-makers use the tools to save time when reviewing asylum cases; when used together, the pilot showed the tools could save around an hour per case, according to government estimates. Caseworkers use the ACS to speed up their review of transcripts of interviews where asylum seekers explain how they were persecuted in their country and why they are afraid to return. They use the APS as a search assistant to find and summarize country policy information, which informs them whether the applicant faces a genuine risk of harm in their home country. In July, a UK judge accused the Home Office of citing an “AI hallucinated” document to refuse a Moroccan woman and her child’s asylum claim on the basis that her home country would be safe for her to return to.

“We’re dealing with people’s lives. We’re talking about people that have faced some of the worst circumstances, and we’re meant to be making decisions based on facts and on understanding harm,” Labour backbench MP Bell Ribeiro-Addy tells WIRED. “I just don’t think it’s appropriate that machines are doing that.”

A Home Office spokesperson says, “Use of Artificial Intelligence is just one of the tools at our disposal to protect our borders, and does not replace or automate the role of human decision-makers.”

Ribeiro-Addy, Alsherif, and the Public Law Project, which has separately been investigating the tools, also worry that well-documented “cultural bias” in GPT models could lead to language barriers and the loss of cultural nuances in the summaries, which could in turn result in discriminatory decisions. An OpenAI spokesperson highlighted to WIRED the company’s ongoing work to improve its models’ accuracy and pointed out that the company will be retiring GPT-4 in January.

In the absence of regulation, the UK’s “AI Playbook” mandates that departments must be transparent about the algorithmic tools they use in decision-making processes and make information on them available to the public, including listing those tools on a public repository. The Home Office’s case summarization and policy search tools are not on that list.

Asylum seekers are also not told when these AI tools are used in their case. “Migrant organizations, legal practitioners, not many of them know about the actual use of this tool,” says Alsherif, who leads ORG’s migrant digital justice program. “So we need to let them know about this, let them know how it works, so they can challenge it.” Not being able to contest an incorrect AI summary of their personal information may breach UK data rights laws, Cloisters lawyers wrote in an independent legal opinion commissioned by ORG. The Home Office states that parts of the decision-making process may involve automation in its privacy notice.

Both groups have sent their findings to UK data regulator, the Information Commission, which is currently investigating the Home Office’s refusal to tell ORG how staff use and were trained to use two AI tools.

Public Law Project senior research fellow Caroline Selman also notes that the ACS and APS tools are just two of the 11 high-risk AI systems that her team has found being used across government but absent from the public repository. She’s concerned there may be more deployed across government that even researchers, let alone the individuals they are being used on, are unaware of.

“Other tools are being used but not being publicized at all,” says Selman, “and you can’t even begin to ask questions about things if you don’t know that they’re being used.”

items.summary_zh: 英国边境和移民独立首席监察长正考虑对内政部使用OpenAI生成式AI工具处理庇护申请的行为展开调查

ai_analysis.briefing_zh: 英国边境和移民独立首席监察长（ICIBI）正考虑对英国内政部使用生成式AI工具处理难民庇护申请的行为展开正式调查。此前，数字权利非营利组织“开放权利集团”（ORG）通过长达六个月的调查和多次公开记录请求，揭露了内政部在秘密使用AI工具过程中对准确性和透明度的隐瞒，引发了议员和研究人员的广泛质疑。

英国政府监管机构正在考虑对内政部使用生成式人工智能工具处理庇护申请的情况进行调查。在可能的调查之前，立法者和研究人员公开质疑这些工具的准确性以及政府对其使用的保密性。

活动人士萨拉·阿尔谢里夫 (Sara Alsherif) 告诉《连线》杂志，负责监督内政部边境、移民和海关管理的边境和移民独立首席监察员 (ICIBI) 已要求数字版权非营利组织开放权利组织 (ORG) 分享有关这些工具的更多信息，以制定明年将检查的主题计划。 ORG 的调查结果来自对这些工具进行的为期 6 个月的调查，其中涉及 11 个议会问题、两封部长信件和 10 份公共记录请求，这些请求试图从内政部窃取详细信息，而内政部一直隐瞒了有关这些工具的详细信息。

ICIBI 告诉《连线》杂志，在发布年度检查重点之前，它无法确认正在积极考虑哪些主题，但它表示，它意识到人们对人工智能工具使用的担忧，并指出去年的调查结果表明，其中一个工具的“有效性和可靠性各不相同”。

“庇护决定是由训练有素的个案工作者做出的，人工智能工具仅用于协助浏览面谈记录和政策信息。它们不能单独使用，也不会对申请做出决定，”内政部发言人在一封电子邮件中告诉《连线》杂志。 “我们定期监控这些工具的性能以及我们既定的质量保证流程，并已承诺在其推出时发布更新的评估。”

根据 ORG 获得的文件，内政部使用基于 OpenAI 2023 GPT-4 大语言模型和 Microsoft Foundry 构建的庇护案件摘要 (ACS) 和庇护政策搜索 (APS) 工具来汇总庇护申请人的面谈笔录及其原籍国信息。移民和执法机构于 2024 年底开始试用这些工具，当时工党政府试图清理积压的约 10 万份庇护案件，同时掌握英国每年收到的数万份新申请。尽管该部门取得了重大进展，截至 6 月份的一年中等待初步决定的人数减少了一半，但针对决定的上诉数量却激增。

研究人员担心人工智能工具的准确性，尤其是决定是否将某人送回他们担心遭受迫害的国家这样的高风险问题。 ORG 发现，ACS 生成的摘要中被认为不适合使用的百分比（通常是因为它们包含事实错误或虚假陈述）明显高于试点评估中计算出的公布的 9% 错误率。它还发现，APS 生成的摘要没有质量控制。

庇护决策者在审查庇护案件时使用这些工具来节省时间；据政府估计，当一起使用时，试点表明这些工具每个案例可以节省大约一个小时。个案工作者使用 ACS 来加快审查访谈笔录，寻求庇护者在访谈笔录中解释了他们在自己国家如何受到迫害以及他们害怕回国的原因。他们使用 APS 作为搜索助手来查找和总结国家政策信息，从而了解申请人在其祖国是否面临真正的伤害风险。 7月，一名英国法官指责内政部援引一份“人工智能幻觉”文件拒绝一名摩洛哥妇女及其孩子的庇护申请，理由是她可以安全返回祖国。

工党后座议员贝尔·里贝罗-阿迪 (Bell Ribeiro-Addy) 告诉《连线》杂志：“我们正在处理人们的生活。我们谈论的是那些面临过最糟糕情况的人们，我们应该根据事实和了解伤害来做出决定。” “我只是认为机器这样做是不合适的。”

内政部发言人表示：“人工智能的使用只是我们可以用来保护边境的工具之一，并不能取代或自动化人类决策者的角色。”

Ribeiro-Addy、Alsherif 和公法项目分别对这些工具进行了调查，他们还担心 GPT 模型中记录充分的“文化偏见”可能会导致语言障碍和摘要中文化细微差别的丧失，从而可能导致歧视性决策。 OpenAI 发言人向 WIRED 强调了该公司为提高模型准确性所做的持续努力，并指出该公司将于 1 月份停用 GPT-4。

在缺乏监管的情况下，英国的“人工智能手册”要求各部门必须对其在决策过程中使用的算法工具保持透明，并向公众提供有关这些工具的信息，包括在公共存储库中列出这些工具。内政部的案例总结和政策搜索工具不在该列表中。

寻求庇护者也不会被告知何时在他们的案件中使用这些人工智能工具。 “移民组织、法律从业者中，没有多少人知道这个工具的实际用途，”ORG 移民数字司法项目的负责人阿尔谢里夫说。 “所以我们需要让他们知道这一点，让他们知道它是如何运作的，这样他们就可以挑战它。” Cloisters 律师在 ORG 委托的一份独立法律意见中写道，无法对人工智能对其个人信息的错误摘要提出质疑可能违反英国数据权利法。内政部在其隐私声明中表示，部分决策过程可能涉及自动化。

两个组织都已将调查结果发送给英国数据监管机构信息委员会，该委员会目前正在调查内政部拒绝告诉 ORG 员工如何使用两种人工智能工具并接受培训的情况。

公法项目高级研究员 Caroline Selman 还指出，ACS 和 APS 工具只是她的团队发现的 11 个高风险人工智能系统中的两个，这些系统在政府范围内使用，但公共存储库中却没有。她担心政府可能会部署更多的人员，甚至连研究人员都没有意识到，更不用说他们所使用的个人了。

“其他工具正在被使用，但根本没有被公开，”塞尔曼说，“如果你不知道它们正在被使用，你甚至无法开始提出问题。”

items.title: Retell uses OpenAI models to help power 100M monthly calls
items.title_en: Retell uses OpenAI models to help power 100M monthly calls
items.author: OpenAI 官方动态
items.original_content: GPT-6 Astra tops Retell’s voice agent benchmark, while Codex helps it reach a $1.6M annual revenue run rate per employee.
items.content_snippet: GPT-6 Astra tops Retell’s voice agent benchmark, while Codex helps it reach a $1.6M annual revenue run rate per employee.
items.summary_en: A conversational voice agent platform revealed that by embedding next-generation flagship reasoning and coding models, it now handles over 100 million voice calls each month. Powered by this underlying infrastructure, the startup secured top rankings in voice agent benchmarks while generating an extraordinary $1.6 million in annual run-rate revenue per employee. The milestone illustrates how ultra-lean technical teams can achieve unprecedented operating leverage by building directly atop frontier AI models.
items.title_zh: 语音智能体月呼叫破亿：初创企业人均年创收千万
items.summary_zh: 初创企业全面引入下一代大模型赋能语音智能体，实现单月承接一亿次呼叫且员工人均创收突破千万人民币

ai_analysis.briefing_zh: 智能化通信服务平台宣布全面接入新一代前沿旗舰模型与代码引擎，依托该技术其语音智能体每月承接的真实通话量已正式突破一亿次大关。在先进模型的推理支持下，该平台不仅在语音交互基准测试中占据榜首，更实现了单个全职员工对应高达一百六十万美元年化营收的惊人运营杠杆。这一技术应用实例充分展现了极端精简的工程团队通过调用高阶大模型基础设施，在垂直场景爆发出的超常商业转化效能。

Powered by this underlying infrastructure, the startup secured top rankings in voice agent benchmarks while generating an extraordinary $1.6 million in annual run-rate revenue per employee. The milestone illustrates how ultra-lean technical teams can achieve unprecedented operating leverage by building directly atop frontier AI models.

ai_analysis.insight_zh: 人均年创收千万的狂欢背后，是成千上万个传统客服坐席饭碗被悄无声息地击碎。以前大厂吹嘘以人为本，现在创业公司最骄傲的战绩，是全公司除了几个看管服务器的工程师，整个运转系统里根本不需要活人。
ai_analysis.insight_en: Behind the headline celebration of $1.6 million revenue per employee is the silent obsolescence of thousands of customer support call centers. Silicon Valley used to brag about empowering teams; today's badge of honor is showing a balance sheet where human labor has been almost entirely optimized away.

items.title: Former Deepmind researcher thinks AlphaGo's playbook can cure AI hallucinations
items.title_en: Former Deepmind researcher thinks AlphaGo's playbook can cure AI hallucinations
items.author: THE DECODER
items.article_content:
Former Deepmind researcher Thore Graepel wants his startup Metis Reasoning to bring AlphaGo's search principle to general reasoning. Instead of locking knowledge inside model weights, an explicit knowledge ledger would make every conclusion checkable against evidence. So far, though, there's no working system and no benchmarks.

The article Former Deepmind researcher thinks AlphaGo's playbook can cure AI hallucinations appeared first on The Decoder.

items.summary_en: Former DeepMind researcher Thore Graepel has founded Metis Reasoning to bring AlphaGo's search principles to general reasoning, utilizing an explicit knowledge ledger to make every AI conclusion verifiable against evidence rather than locking knowledge in weights.
items.title_zh: 前DeepMind研究员拟用AlphaGo逻辑解决幻觉
items.summary_zh: 前DeepMind研究员Thore Graepel创立初创公司Metis Reasoning，试图将AlphaGo的搜索原则引入大模型以根治幻觉

ai_analysis.briefing_zh: 前DeepMind研究员Thore Graepel近日创立了名为Metis Reasoning的初创公司，旨在将围棋AI AlphaGo的搜索原则应用到通用推理领域。该方案试图抛弃将全部知识锁在模型权重内的传统做法，通过构建显式知识账本，让每一个AI结论都能与客观证据进行交叉验证，从而从根本上消除大模型幻觉，不过目前该系统尚无可用原型或基准测试。
ai_analysis.briefing_en: Former DeepMind researcher Thore Graepel has founded Metis Reasoning to bring AlphaGo's search principles to general reasoning, utilizing an explicit knowledge ledger to make every AI conclusion verifiable against evidence rather than locking knowledge in weights.

elements_zh.where: AI前沿推理研究领域

elements_zh.why: 为了解决当前大模型将知识锁死在权重中导致不可解释和频繁幻觉的底层缺陷

elements_en.who: Former DeepMind researcher Thore Graepel (Founder of Metis Reasoning)
elements_en.what: Plans to use AlphaGo's search principles and an explicit knowledge ledger to make AI conclusions verifiable
elements_en.why: To solve the fundamental flaw of LLMs locking knowledge in weights, which causes uninterpretability and hallucinations

ai_analysis.insight_zh: 用AlphaGo下围棋那一套穷举搜索来治大模型满嘴跑火车的幻觉，思路极其性感，只可惜现在的PPT离跑通代码还有十万八千里。
ai_analysis.insight_en: Applying AlphaGo’s search playbook to fix LLM hallucinations is a brilliant pitch, but right now the slide deck is light-years ahead of any working code.

items.title: Apple is adding an AI chatbot to Pages, Keynote, and Numbers
items.title_en: Apple is adding an AI chatbot to Pages, Keynote, and Numbers
items.author: The Verge AI
items.article_content:
Apple is bringing an AI assistant to its suite of productivity apps, including Keynote, Pages, and Numbers. The assistant, which is built on AI models from Apple and OpenAI, can understand a document's context to perform tasks like designing, animating, and refining slides in Keynote.

In Pages, Apple says the AI assistant can draft, restructure, and tweak written content. It can also calculate, visualize, and organize data in Numbers, while suggesting chart types and building custom tables.

Keynote, Pages, and Numbers now support the Model Context Protocol on macOS 27 or later, allowing third-party AI agents to plug into the apps. The AI  …

items.title: Neocloud General Compute, which specializes in bare-metal infrastructure, raised a $100M Series A led by Blackbird and Abstract at an $800M post-money valuation (Tim Fernholz/TechCrunch)
items.title_en: Neocloud General Compute, which specializes in bare-metal infrastructure, raised a $100M Series A led by Blackbird and Abstract at an $800M post-money valuation (Tim Fernholz/TechCrunch)
items.author: TechCrunch
items.article_content:
CoreWeave, a publicly traded neocloud that rents out computing power for AI, has seen its stock price fall to a 12-month low, and Elon Musk is flexing $40 billion in debt for buying computing capacity and predicting that “200+ neoclouds are going to see guppy-level death and consolidation.” It’s not exactly the ideal week to announce a Series A for a neocloud.

General Compute co-founder and CEO Finn Puklowski is unfazed. He’s bullish on CoreWeave’s chances, and thinks Musk is just talking his book to drive down the prices of the GPUs he wants to buy. Fears of a chip-led collapse are “massively overstated. I have people calling me up every single week asking me to do TPUs, GPUs, any chip, to get them more compute.”

Just as important, he says, Anthropic’s bullish S-1 is “settling fears for today.”

General Compute has found a niche building its cloud out of specialized inference chips built by Nvidia rivals. The company struck a $400 million deal to purchase new chips from SambaNova—the first debt financing of inference chips—and now has added Positron and Cerebras to its portfolio of chip suppliers.

A deal with a large customer worth $100 million in annual recurring revenue has paved the way for the company to raise $100 million in Series A funding led by Blackbird Ventures and Abstract Ventures. Valued at $60 million after a May seed round, General Compute is now worth $800 million post-money to its investors.

The startup’s strategy is to zig where others zag. It focused on chips built for inference while everyone else chased GPUs. And instead of taking on a complex effort to build huge data centers, it uses smaller power sources, rents space in other companies’ data centers, and converts former bitcoin-mining sites into places that run AI models.

That approach means General Compute isn’t going to catapult into the top ranks of neoclouds or compete with hyperscalers any time soon. But it’s also not subject to the constraints that come with building data centers from scratch. When General Compute has chips, it will have someplace to plug them in. Puklowski expects the company to deploy 75 megawatts of computing capacity in 2027, and he suspects he will have access to 200 megawatts of power—“more than we can probably fund and get hardware for.”

Still, the plan has a limit. Puklowski’s financing work isn’t done—”capital is going to be a full-time job for me, both on debt and equity,” he told TechCrunch.

The startup has found key customers in cloud companies that specialize in offering developers high-speed inference; General Compute provides the bare metal, or raw servers with no software layered on top, for them to bring their offerings to market. James Palmer, a principal at Blackbird who co-led the round, said his firm’s confidence in General Compute comes in part from an investment in Baseten, an inference cloud company.

“We’ve been proximate to their journey over the last 10 months and observing the wild growth story that [Baseten] has gone on, and the demand for open weight inference, and for companies owning their own intelligence,” Palmer told TechCrunch. When it comes to General Compute, he said, “Cerebras, Positron, SambaNova, all need distribution partners who can take them to scale, who can navigate the complexity of the physical world.”

Executives at all three chipmakers sang General Compute’s praises to TechCrunch, each noting the importance of the company’s focus on making the economics of AI cloud compute work. “Everyone in this market is selling speed,” Rodrigo Liang, SambaNova’s CEO and co-founder, said. “The real question is whether you can make money doing it.”

items.article_content_zh:
CoreWeave 是一家为 AI 出租计算能力的公开交易 Neocloud，其股价已跌至 12 个月低点，而埃隆·马斯克 (Elon Musk) 正在举债 400 亿美元购买计算能力，并预测“200 多个 Neocloud 将出现孔雀鱼级别的消亡和整合”。这并不是宣布 Neocloud A 轮融资的理想时机。

General Compute 联合创始人兼首席执行官 Finn Puklowski 并不担心。他看好 CoreWeave 的机会，并认为马斯克只是在谈论他的书，以压低他想要购买的 GPU 的价格。对芯片主导的崩溃的担忧“被严重夸大了。每周都会有人打电话给我，要求我做 TPU、GPU 或任何芯片，以获得更多的计算能力。”

他说，同样重要的是，Anthropic 的看涨 S-1 正在“消除今天的担忧”。

General Compute 已经找到了一个利基市场，利用 Nvidia 竞争对手制造的专用推理芯片构建其云。该公司达成了一项价值 4 亿美元的交易，从 SambaNova 购买新芯片，这是推理芯片的首笔债务融资，现在已将 Positron 和 Cerebras 添加到其芯片供应商组合中。

与年经常性收入达 1 亿美元的大客户达成的交易，为该公司在 Blackbird Ventures 和 Abstract Ventures 领投的 A 轮融资中筹集 1 亿美元铺平了道路。 General Compute 在 5 月份的种子轮融资后估值为 6000 万美元，目前对投资者而言，投后估值为 8 亿美元。

这家初创公司的战略是在其他公司曲折的地方曲折前进。它专注于为推理而构建的芯片，而其他人都在追逐 GPU。它没有采取复杂的努力来建设大型数据中心，而是使用较小的电源，租用其他公司数据中心的空间，并将以前的比特币挖矿站点转变为运行人工智能模型的地方。

这种方法意味着通用计算不会很快跻身新云的顶级行列或与超大规模企业竞争。但它也不受从头开始构建数据中心所带来的限制。当 General Compute 拥有芯片时，就会有地方插入它们。Puklowski 预计该公司将在 2027 年部署 75 兆瓦的计算能力，他怀疑自己将获得 200 兆瓦的电力——“这超出了我们可能资助和购买硬件的能力。”

不过，该计划也有其局限性。普克洛斯基的融资工作还没有完成——“资本对我来说将是一份全职工作，无论是债务还是股权，”他告诉 TechCrunch。

该初创公司在专门为开发人员提供高速推理的云公司中找到了关键客户； General Compute 提供裸机或原始服务器，顶部没有软件层，以便他们将产品推向市场。 Blackbird 的负责人、本轮融资的共同领投人 James Palmer 表示，他的公司对 General Compute 的信心部分来自于对推理云公司 Baseten 的投资。

“我们在过去 10 个月里一直密切关注他们的发展历程，观察 [Baseten] 的疯狂增长故事，以及对开放权重推理的需求，以及对拥有自己的情报的公司的需求，”帕尔默告诉 TechCrunch。谈到通用计算，他说：“Cerebras、Positron、SambaNova 都需要能够扩大规模、能够驾驭物理世界复杂性的分销合作伙伴。”

三大芯片制造商的高管都对 TechCrunch 表示了对 General Compute 的赞扬，他们都指出了该公司专注于使 AI 云计算经济发挥作用的重要性。 “这个市场上的每个人都在追求销售速度，”SambaNova 首席执行官兼联合创始人罗德里戈·梁 (Rodrigo Liang) 表示。 “真正的问题是你是否能通过这样做赚钱。”

Anduril and Qualcomm unveil BlueChip, a line of laptops designed and assembled in the US for defense and government; Anduril will begin taking orders in 2027  —  Defense tech startup Anduril Industries Inc. has joined forces with chipmaker Qualcomm Inc.
items.content_snippet: Defense tech startup Anduril Industries Inc. has joined forces with chipmaker Qualcomm Inc. to produce laptops that are designed …
items.summary_en: Defense tech startup Anduril partnered with Qualcomm to unveil 'BlueChip,' a line of laptops designed and assembled in the U.S. Targeted at government and defense sectors, the products are expected to be available for order in 2027.
items.title_zh: Anduril发布美产防务笔记本
items.summary_zh: 防务初创Anduril与高通合作推出BlueChip美产笔记本，专供政府与国防客户，2027年交付

ai_analysis.briefing_zh: 防务科技初创公司Anduril与高通携手，宣布推出BlueChip系列笔记本电脑。该系列主打“美国设计与组装”，旨在为政府及国防安全部门提供安全可靠的移动计算终端，首批产品预计于2027年正式开启预订。
ai_analysis.briefing_en: Defense tech startup Anduril partnered with Qualcomm to unveil 'BlueChip,' a line of laptops designed and assembled in the U.S. Targeted at government and defense sectors, the products are expected to be available for order in 2027.

elements_zh.what: 发布BlueChip美产笔记本系列
elements_zh.why: 响应地缘政治下国防供应链回流及硬件安全可控的需求

elements_en.what: Unveiled BlueChip, a U.S.-made laptop line
elements_en.why: To address the demand for domestic, secure supply chains in defense technology

ai_analysis.insight_zh: 现在连笔记本都要讲“血统”了。这哪是卖电脑，这是卖一种“防间谍”的安全感，毕竟在国防订单里，高通的芯片加上美国制造的组装费，那可是溢价的黄金组合。
ai_analysis.insight_en: Laptops now come with 'pedigree' requirements. This isn't just about hardware; it's about selling the feeling of being 'spy-proof'—because for government contracts, a Qualcomm chip and a 'Made in USA' label is the ultimate premium combo.
